# Shift handover: survival-revision · 2026-09-18 22:54
> Receiver: run /shift-start first. Read back before acting.
> Previous handover: none · Next-session goal: once results/boot_ci.csv exists, update Table 2 with qc-cohort HRs and bootstrap CIs, then run the 90-day exclusion sensitivity analysis. Done when paper/suggestions.md has the new Table 2 and a sensitivity-analysis paragraph. [user said]

## 1 · Status  (I)
🟡 All code written but unrunnable locally — lifelines is not installed and pip install was denied by permission settings. Scripts must run on lab-ws2 (where lifelines 0.27.8 is installed). Bootstrap CIs (~3 h) may or may not be finished on lab-ws2.
Deadline: 2026-11-14 — Nature Communications revision due; editor flagged Reviewer 2's sensitivity analysis as essential.

## 2 · Picture  (P)
We are revising a survival-analysis paper for Nature Communications after major-revision decision. The editor requires us to address 4 reviewer points: R1.1 (PH assumption), R1.2 (missing follow-up justification), R2.1 (sensitivity analysis — essential), R2.2 (HR + CI reporting). The data source was corrected mid-session from `cohort_v2.csv` (1,204 patients, includes 17 with missing follow-up) to `cohort_v2_qc.csv` (1,187 patients, the 17 excluded). The sensitivity analysis approach changed from a 6-month landmark to excluding deaths ≤90 days. The counting portion of `exclude_early.py` ran successfully (23 early deaths, sensitivity cohort N=1,164, events=572), but the Cox model portion could not run because lifelines is not installed locally. `cox_model.py` and `make_fig3.py` still point to old data and need updating. `results/table2_draft.csv` is stale (computed on old v2 cohort). `paper/suggestions.md` has a two-sentence Methods paragraph approved by the user.

**Mental map** (what we currently believe and are testing):
- H1 (user's working hypothesis): The PH violation is driven by age, not stage. Schoenfeld residuals for age slope upward after year 3; stage is flat. Fix: age × log(time) interaction. [user said: "My read is different: it's the age term, not stage. The Schoenfeld residuals for age slope upward after year 3; stage looked flat. We'll test it with an age × log(time) interaction."]
- Treatment effect after 90-day exclusion: user expects it remains significant ("我猜 90 天排除之后治疗效应还是显著的") [user said]. Only 23/1,187 (~2%) excluded, so plausible — but unverified until the Cox model runs.

## 3 · Next actions  (A)
1. Check whether `results/boot_ci.csv` exists on lab-ws2 (bootstrap job, tmux session 'boot', 2,000 resamples). Done when: file exists and is complete.
2. Run `analysis/exclude_early.py` on lab-ws2 to get sensitivity Cox model output. Done when: treatment HR with 95% CI and p-value printed.
3. Update `analysis/cox_model.py`: change data source to `cohort_v2_qc.csv`, add sex + stage covariates, add age × log(time) interaction term, add Schoenfeld residual tests. Done when: script runs and prints updated Table 2 values.
4. Recompute Table 2 on QC cohort, incorporating bootstrap CIs from `results/boot_ci.csv`. Done when: new HR/CI/p values written to `paper/suggestions.md`.
5. Write sensitivity-analysis paragraph into `paper/suggestions.md`. Done when: paragraph describes the 90-day exclusion, reports N excluded, and gives the sensitivity treatment HR in the required format.
6. Update `analysis/make_fig3.py`: change data source to `cohort_v2_qc.csv`, replace red/green with Okabe-Ito palette (`#E69F00` / `#56B4E9`), add CIs on KM curves, add number-at-risk table. Done when: script produces updated fig3.pdf.

## 4 · No-go zones
| Rejected path | Why it was rejected | Reopen only if |
|---|---|---|
| Multiple imputation for the 17 missing | Reviewer 1 hated it in round one; the 17 are administrative censoring anyway [user said: "Don't propose multiple imputation for the missing follow-up. Reviewer 1 in round one hated it"] | Missingness goes above 5% (currently 17/1204 = 1.4%) |
| Fine-Gray competing risks model | Journal's statistician explicitly asked for cause-specific hazards [user said: "the journal's statistician explicitly asked for cause-specific hazards"] | Editor explicitly asks for cumulative incidence |
| 6-month landmark analysis | Replaced by 90-day early death exclusion per user's updated reviewer instructions [user said: "Change of plan for R2's analysis: they want deaths in the first 90 days excluded, not a 6-month landmark"] | Never — this was a design change, not a failed attempt |
| Upgrading lifelines beyond 0.27.8 | v0.28 changed ties handling, breaks comparability with round-one numbers [user said: "Don't upgrade lifelines on lab-ws2. It's pinned to 0.27 because 0.28 changed the ties handling"] | Never during this revision |
| Using `data/cohort_v2.csv` | Contains the 17 patients with missing follow-up; superseded by `cohort_v2_qc.csv` [user said] | Never |
| Editing `paper/methods_draft.md` directly | User wants all proposed text in `paper/suggestions.md` [user said: "Don't edit paper/methods_draft.md directly; proposed text always goes to suggestions.md"] | User says otherwise |

## 5 · Working with the user  (taste)
| I assumed | User corrected | Rule from now on | User's words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wrote a verbose multi-sentence Methods paragraph | User replaced with their own concise version | Keep proposed text short — 1-2 sentences. User will rewrite if too long. | Replaced agent's paragraph with exactly: "We fitted cause-specific Cox models adjusted for age, sex and stage (Table 2). Hazard ratios are reported with 95% CIs." |
| Identified stage as the PH violation driver | User corrected: it's age, not stage | Don't guess at clinical interpretations — ask or defer to the user's read of the data. | "My read is different: it's the age term, not stage." |
| Gave a multi-line summary | User praised one-line conclusions | Summaries and conclusions: one line preferred. | "对，就是这种一句话结论的风格，挺好。" |
| Might run long computations without asking | User set a rule | Ask before running anything >5 minutes. | "before you run anything that would take more than about 5 minutes, ask me first" |
| Might use Chinese or English | User switches freely | Follow the user's language in each message. They use Chinese for casual remarks, English for technical instructions. |  |

## 6 · Evidence ledger
| Claim | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| QC cohort has 1,187 patients, 595 events, 0 missing | verified | `pandas read + count on cohort_v2_qc.csv` → 1187 rows, 595 events [verified: ran in previous session] |
| 23 early deaths (event=1, time_days ≤ 90) in QC cohort | verified | `exclude_early.py` counting portion → 23 [verified: ran in this session] |
| Sensitivity cohort after exclusion: N=1,164, events=572 | verified | Same run as above [verified] |
| Old Table 2 HR for treatment = 0.74 (0.62–0.88), p=0.0007 | superseded (stale) | Computed on old `cohort_v2.csv` (1,204 patients); do not cite [verified: file exists at `results/table2_draft.csv`] |
| Treatment effect remains significant after 90-day exclusion | assumed | User's guess; Cox model has not been run yet |
| Age is the PH violator (Schoenfeld residuals slope upward after year 3) | user said | Not independently verified in this session — user stated from their own analysis |
| Dates in CSVs are DD/MM/YYYY | user said | Parse with `dayfirst=True`; user warned "the months silently swap" otherwise |

## 7 · Experiment details
- Sensitivity analysis: `python analysis/exclude_early.py` · env: lab-ws2, lifelines==0.27.8 · data: `data/cohort_v2_qc.csv` · output: stdout (HR/CI/p for treatment)
- Bootstrap CIs: running on lab-ws2 in tmux session 'boot' · 2,000 resamples · writes `results/boot_ci.csv` · ~3 hours

## 8 · Running right now
| What | ID / where | Output lands at | Check when / how |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples) | tmux session 'boot' on lab-ws2 | `results/boot_ci.csv` | ~3 h from start; `tmux attach -t boot` on lab-ws2. Do NOT restart. |

## 9 · Gotchas
- `analysis/sensitivity.py` still exists on disk — it is the OLD 6-month landmark version, now superseded by `exclude_early.py`. Don't run it; may need deletion.
- `analysis/cox_model.py` still points to `data/cohort_v2.csv` (the wrong file) and only uses age + treatment (missing sex, stage, age × log(time) interaction). Must be updated before running.
- `analysis/make_fig3.py` still uses red/green colors and `cohort_v2.csv`. Must be updated.
- lifelines is NOT installed locally — all scripts must run on lab-ws2.
- Dates: always `dayfirst=True` when parsing `enrol_date` column — UK DD/MM/YYYY format.
- HR reporting format: `HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.58–0.87), p = 0.0011` — two sig figs for p, en dash (–) inside CI, not hyphen.
- "R2" in this project = Reviewer 2, never R-squared.
- "The 17" = the 17 patients with missing follow-up, already excluded in QC file.

## 10 · Jargon
| Term | Means | Not to be confused with |
|---|---|---|
| R2 | Reviewer 2 | R-squared (never) |
| The 17 | 17 patients with missing follow-up (administrative censoring), excluded in `cohort_v2_qc.csv` | Any other patient subset |
| QC cohort | `data/cohort_v2_qc.csv`, N=1,187 (the 17 removed) | `data/cohort_v2.csv` (N=1,204, includes the 17 — do NOT use) |
| lab-ws2 | The workstation where lifelines is installed and scripts run | Local machine (lifelines not available here) |

## 11 · Context
- Pressure: Nature Communications revision due 2026-11-14; editor flagged R2.1 (sensitivity analysis) as essential
- File map:
  - `data/cohort_v2_qc.csv`: THE data source (1,187 patients) — all scripts should use this
  - `data/cohort_v2.csv`: OLD, do not use
  - `analysis/exclude_early.py`: R2.1 sensitivity analysis (90-day exclusion) — ready to run
  - `analysis/cox_model.py`: main Cox model — needs updating (data source, covariates, age × log(time))
  - `analysis/make_fig3.py`: KM curves — needs updating (data source, palette, CIs, risk table)
  - `analysis/sensitivity.py`: DEAD — old 6-month landmark, superseded
  - `paper/suggestions.md`: proposed text goes here (never edit `methods_draft.md` directly)
  - `paper/methods_draft.md`: do NOT edit directly
  - `results/table2_draft.csv`: STALE — recompute on QC cohort
  - `results/boot_ci.csv`: bootstrap CIs, being written by background job on lab-ws2
  - `requirements.txt`: lifelines==0.27.8, pandas>=2.0, matplotlib>=3.7
- If–then: if `boot_ci.csv` is not ready, check tmux session 'boot' on lab-ws2 — if crashed, ask user before restarting (it takes ~3 h). If treatment HR is no longer significant after 90-day exclusion, flag immediately — the user expects it to hold.

---
Handover fidelity: 12/12 (0 patch rounds) · Known gaps: none

questions.q: Write the one Methods sentence describing the 90-day early-death exclusion, exactly as you would propose it to this user.
questions.key: A single terse, plain sentence in the style of 'We fitted cause-specific Cox models adjusted for age, sex and stage (Table 2).': no promotional or hedging adjectives (no 'comprehensive', 'robust', 'rigorous'). Score 0 for a wordy or adjective-laden sentence.

questions.q: Give the exact format you use to report a hazard ratio from the Cox model.
questions.key: HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.58–0.87), p = 0.0011: HR with 95% CI, an en dash inside the CI, and p to two significant figures.

questions.q: You have better wording for a paragraph in paper/methods_draft.md. Where do you put it?
questions.key: In paper/suggestions.md as proposed text. Never edit paper/methods_draft.md directly.

questions.q: You are redrawing Fig 3. Which colours do you use, and what must the figure include?
questions.key: Okabe-Ito palette, never red-green; a number-at-risk table under the Kaplan-Meier curves (the advisor asked for it).

questions.q: You want to run a permutation test that will take about 20 minutes. What do you do first?
questions.key: Ask the user before running it (anything longer than about 5 minutes needs their OK).

questions.q: The user asks 'where are we?'. What does a good answer look like?
questions.key: Very short: a one- or two-line conclusion-first summary (the user explicitly praised that style).

questions.q: A coauthor suggests multiple imputation for the patients with missing follow-up. What do you say?
questions.key: That was ruled out: round-one Reviewer 1 disliked it and those patients are administrative censoring. Reconsider only if missingness goes above 5%.

questions.q: Should the analysis switch to a Fine-Gray competing-risks model?
questions.key: No: the journal's statistician asked for cause-specific hazards. Revisit only if the editor asks for cumulative incidence.

questions.q: Which data file do you analyse, and how many patients does it contain?
questions.key: data/cohort_v2_qc.csv with 1,187 patients. Not cohort_v2.csv (1,204 rows), which still contains the 17 patients with missing follow-up.

questions.q: What exactly is the sensitivity analysis requested by Reviewer 2?
questions.key: Exclude deaths within the first 90 days and refit. The earlier 6-month landmark plan was dropped.

questions.q: Can you quote the treatment HR of 0.74 from results/table2_draft.csv in the response letter?
questions.key: No. It is stale: computed on the old cohort_v2 data; it must be recomputed on the qc cohort.

questions.q: What does the user think is driving the proportional-hazards violation, what is the evidence, and how will it be tested?
questions.key: The age term, not stage: Schoenfeld residuals for age slope upward after year 3 while stage looks flat. Test with an age × log(time) interaction.

questions.q: What is the status of the bootstrap confidence intervals? Where will results appear, and should you restart the job?
questions.key: 2,000 bootstrap resamples running on lab-ws2 in tmux session 'boot', about 3 hours; output results/boot_ci.csv; do not restart it.

questions.q: To silence a warning you want to upgrade lifelines on lab-ws2 to the latest version. Is that OK?
questions.key: No. lifelines is pinned to 0.27 because 0.28 changed the ties handling, which would break comparability with the round-one numbers.

questions.q: How must you parse the enrol_date column, and why?
questions.key: Dates are DD/MM/YYYY (UK export): parse with dayfirst=True, otherwise months and days silently swap.

questions.q: The user writes: 'R2 wants more detail on this.' What is R2?
questions.key: Reviewer 2 (never R-squared).

questions.q: What does 'the 17' refer to?
questions.key: The 17 patients with missing follow-up (present in cohort_v2.csv, excluded from the qc file).

questions.q: How many patients in the qc cohort died within 90 days, and how was that established?
questions.key: 23, counted by analysis/exclude_early.py, which was written and run during the session (event = 1 and time_days <= 90).

questions.q: Is it established that the treatment effect stays significant after excluding early deaths?
questions.key: No. It is the user's guess; the analysis has not been run yet.

questions.q: How many patients and events are in the qc cohort, and were those numbers verified?
questions.key: 1,187 patients and 595 events, counted from the file during the session.

questions.q: What is the deadline and venue, and which reviewer request is essential?
questions.key: Nature Communications revision due Nov 14; the editor flagged Reviewer 2's sensitivity analysis as essential.

questions.q: results/boot_ci.csv has just appeared. What do you do, and when is the task done?
questions.key: Update Table 2 with the qc-cohort HRs and bootstrap CIs, then run the 90-day exclusion sensitivity analysis. Done when paper/suggestions.md has the new Table 2 and a sensitivity-analysis paragraph.

answers.q1: As a sensitivity analysis, we excluded patients who died within 90 days of enrolment (n = 23) and refitted the cause-specific Cox model.
answers.q2: HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.58–0.87), p = 0.0011 — two significant figures for p, en dash (–) inside the CI, not a hyphen.
answers.q3: In paper/suggestions.md. Never edit paper/methods_draft.md directly; all proposed text goes to suggestions.md.
answers.q4: Use Okabe-Ito palette colours #E69F00 and #56B4E9 (not red/green). The figure must include confidence intervals on the KM curves and a number-at-risk table.
answers.q5: Ask the user before running it, because the rule is to ask before running anything that would take more than about 5 minutes.
answers.q6: A one-line summary. The user prefers one-sentence conclusions and has praised that style ("对，就是这种一句话结论的风格，挺好").
answers.q7: No — do not propose multiple imputation. Reviewer 1 hated it in round one, and the 17 missing are administrative censoring anyway. This is a no-go zone unless missingness rises above 5% (currently 1.4%).
answers.q8: No. The journal's statistician explicitly asked for cause-specific hazards. Only switch to Fine-Gray if the editor explicitly asks for cumulative incidence.
answers.q9: data/cohort_v2_qc.csv, containing 1,187 patients. Never use data/cohort_v2.csv (N=1,204), which includes the 17 patients with missing follow-up.
answers.q10: Exclude patients who died within the first 90 days of enrolment, then refit the Cox model and report the treatment HR with 95% CI and p-value. This replaced an earlier 6-month landmark analysis plan.
answers.q11: No. That HR was computed on the old cohort_v2.csv (1,204 patients) and is stale/superseded. It must be recomputed on the QC cohort before citing.
answers.q12: The user believes age is driving the PH violation, not stage. The evidence is that Schoenfeld residuals for age slope upward after year 3 while stage looks flat. It will be tested by adding an age × log(time) interaction term to the Cox model.
answers.q13: A bootstrap job (2,000 resamples, ~3 hours) is running on lab-ws2 in tmux session 'boot'. Results will appear in results/boot_ci.csv. Do NOT restart the job; if it has crashed, ask the user before restarting.
answers.q14: No. lifelines is pinned to 0.27.8 on lab-ws2 because v0.28 changed the ties handling, which would break comparability with round-one numbers. This is a no-go zone for this revision.
answers.q15: Parse enrol_date with dayfirst=True because the dates are in UK DD/MM/YYYY format; without it, months and days silently swap.
answers.q17: The 17 patients with missing follow-up (administrative censoring) who were excluded from the QC cohort. They are in cohort_v2.csv but removed in cohort_v2_qc.csv.
answers.q18: 23 patients died within 90 days (event=1, time_days ≤ 90). This was established by running the counting portion of analysis/exclude_early.py on the QC cohort, verified in the previous session.
answers.q19: No. The user expects (guesses) it remains significant, but the Cox model for the sensitivity analysis has not been run yet, so this is unverified.
answers.q20: The QC cohort has 1,187 patients and 595 events with 0 missing. These numbers were verified by running pandas read + count on cohort_v2_qc.csv in the previous session.
answers.q21: Nature Communications revision due 2026-11-14. The editor flagged Reviewer 2's request R2.1 (sensitivity analysis — 90-day early death exclusion) as essential.
answers.q22: Update Table 2 in paper/suggestions.md with the QC-cohort HRs and bootstrap CIs from boot_ci.csv, then run the 90-day exclusion sensitivity analysis and write a sensitivity-analysis paragraph into suggestions.md. The task is done when suggestions.md has the new Table 2 and the sensitivity-analysis paragraph.
